- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing reversal.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.00 to -1.00 within 3 days), model fails to adjust quickly; apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day of sentiment divergence.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows low volatility, model often overfits recent noise; use 10-day smoothing filter before forecasting.
